method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the measles chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Free to read, not CC BY; quoted with attribution. ⚠️ The immunoglobulin post-exposure doses and the CDNA measles guidelines were NOT extracted.

claims.claim: CHILDREN: ALL CHILDREN AGED 12 MONTHS AND OVER are recommended 2 DOSES of measles-containing vaccine — MMR AT 12 MONTHS AND MMRV AT 18 MONTHS
claims.source_text: All children aged ≥12 months are recommended to receive 2 doses of measles-containing vaccine. … 12 months of age — MMR 18 months of age — MMRV
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ WHY NOT BEFORE 12 MONTHS: measles-containing vaccines are NOT ROUTINELY RECOMMENDED FOR INFANTS UNDER 12 MONTHS, because MATERNAL ANTIBODIES PERSIST IN MANY INFANTS AFTER BIRTH, declining over the first year, and MAY INTERFERE WITH ACTIVE IMMUNISATION
claims.source_text: Measles-containing vaccines are not routinely recommended for infants <12 months of age. This is because maternal antibodies to measles persist in many infants after birth, declining progressively over the first year of life. These may interfere with active immunisation before 12 months of age.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ ADULTS: ALL ADOLESCENTS AND ADULTS BORN DURING OR SINCE 1966 should have DOCUMENTED EVIDENCE OF 2 DOSES given AT LEAST 4 WEEKS APART with BOTH GIVEN AT 12 MONTHS OR OLDER, OR SEROLOGICAL EVIDENCE OF IMMUNITY to measles, mumps and rubella. Particularly: HEALTHCARE WORKERS, CHILDHOOD EDUCATORS AND CARERS, LONG-TERM CARE AND CORRECTIONAL FACILITY STAFF, AND TRAVELLERS
claims.source_text: All adolescents and adults born during or since 1966 should have either: documented evidence of 2 doses of measles-containing vaccine given at least 4 weeks apart and with both doses given ≥12 months of age, or serological evidence of immunity to measles, mumps and rubella … particularly healthcare workers childhood educators and carers people who work in long-term care facilities people who work in correctional facilities travellers
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ POST-EXPOSURE: NON-IMMUNE PEOPLE EXPOSED TO MEASLES SHOULD RECEIVE MMR (or MMRV in some instances) FOR POST-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS, IDEALLY WITHIN 72 HOURS OF EXPOSURE. The Handbook's outer window for post-exposure prophylaxis is WITHIN 6 DAYS (144 HOURS) OF FIRST EXPOSURE
claims.source_text: Non-immune people who are exposed to measles should receive an MMR vaccine (or MMRV in some instances) for post-exposure prophylaxis , ideally within 72 hours of exposure. … Post-exposure prophylaxis needed within 6 days (144 hours) of 1st exposure for people exposed to measles
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: A child over 12 months who has had 1 dose CAN RECEIVE THE 2ND DOSE EARLIER THAN 18 MONTHS if they have, or are at risk of, CONTACT WITH A PERSON WITH MEASLES, PROVIDED IT HAS BEEN AT LEAST 4 WEEKS SINCE THE 1ST DOSE. ⚠️ MMRV IS NOT ROUTINELY RECOMMENDED AS THE 1ST DOSE IN CHILDREN UNDER 4 YEARS
claims.source_text: Children >12 months of age who have received 1 dose of measles-containing vaccine can receive their 2nd dose earlier that the scheduled 18-month age milestone if: … it has been at least 4 weeks since the 1st dose … MMRV vaccine is not routinely recommended as the 1st dose of MMR -containing vaccine in children aged <4 years
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ PREGNANCY: MMR-CONTAINING VACCINES ARE CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANT WOMEN, and VACCINATED WOMEN SHOULD AVOID PREGNANCY FOR 28 DAYS AFTER VACCINATION. ⚠️ THERE IS NO RISK TO PREGNANT WOMEN FROM CONTACT WITH RECENTLY VACCINATED PEOPLE — THE VACCINE VIRUS IS NOT TRANSMITTED. BREASTFEEDING WOMEN CAN RECEIVE MMR
claims.source_text: MMR -containing vaccines are contraindicated in pregnant women. Vaccinated women should avoid pregnancy for 28 days after vaccination. … There is no risk to pregnant women from contact with people who have recently been vaccinated. The vaccine viruses is not transmitted from vaccinated people to susceptible contacts. … Breastfeeding women can receive MMR vaccines.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ CONTRAINDICATIONS: MMR and MMRV are contraindicated after ANAPHYLAXIS TO A PREVIOUS DOSE OR TO ANY COMPONENT, IN PREGNANCY, and IN PEOPLE WHO ARE SEVERELY IMMUNOCOMPROMISED — they CONTAIN LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUSES
claims.source_text: MMR and MMRV vaccines are contraindicated in people who have had: anaphylaxis after a previous dose of any MMR -containing vaccine anaphylaxis after any component of an MMR -containing vaccine … MMR -containing vaccines contain live attenuated viruses and are contraindicated in people who are immunocompromised
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ IMMUNOGLOBULIN AFTER VACCINATION: people who have had a measles-containing vaccine SHOULD NOT RECEIVE IMMUNOGLOBULIN-CONTAINING PRODUCTS FOR 3 WEEKS AFTER VACCINATION unless the benefits outweigh. ANTI-D IMMUNOGLOBULIN IS THE EXCEPTION — MMR CAN BE GIVEN AT THE SAME TIME AT A DIFFERENT SITE, OR ANY TIME BEFORE OR AFTER, because anti-D does not interfere with the antibody response
claims.source_text: People who have received a measles-containing vaccine should not receive immunoglobulin -containing products for 3 weeks after vaccination … People may receive MMR vaccine at the same time as anti-D immunoglobulin , but at different injection sites. They can also receive MMR vaccine at any time before or after anti-D immunoglobulin . Anti-D immunoglobulin does not interfere with the antibody response to the vaccine.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: TRANSMISSION: incubation is USUALLY 10-14 DAYS. Measles spreads by RESPIRATORY SECRETIONS INCLUDING AEROSOLS. ⚠️ IT IS INFECTIOUS FROM THE START OF THE PRODROME — TYPICALLY 2-4 DAYS BEFORE THE RASH — AND FOR UP TO 4 DAYS AFTER THE RASH APPEARS
claims.source_text: incubation period is usually 10–14 days. … Measles is spread by respiratory secretions, including by aerosols. … It is infectious from the beginning of the prodromal period (typically 2 to 4 days before rash onset) and for up to 4 days after the rash appears.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: CLINICAL FEATURES: a 2-4 DAY PRODROME of FEVER, MALAISE, COUGH, CORYZA AND CONJUNCTIVITIS, then a MACULOPAPULAR RASH THAT TYPICALLY BEGINS ON THE FACE AND UPPER NECK AND THEN BECOMES GENERALISED
claims.source_text: The prodrome lasts 2–4 days. It is characterised by: fever malaise cough coryza conjunctivitis A maculopapular rash typically begins on the face and upper neck, and then becomes generalised.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ COMPLICATIONS: ABOUT 10% OF CASES INVOLVE COMPLICATIONS — OTITIS MEDIA (~9%), PNEUMONIA (~6%), DIARRHOEA (~8%). ⚠️ ACUTE ENCEPHALITIS OCCURS IN 1 PER 1000 CASES WITH 10-15% MORTALITY, AND A HIGH PROPORTION OF SURVIVORS HAVE PERMANENT BRAIN DAMAGE. SUBACUTE SCLEROSING PANENCEPHALITIS IS A LATE COMPLICATION, ON AVERAGE 7 YEARS AFTER INFECTION
claims.source_text: About 10% of measles cases involve complications. … otitis media (in around 9% of people) pneumonia (in around 6%) diarrhoea (in around 8%) Acute encephalitis occurs in 1 per 1000 cases, and has a mortality rate of 10–15%. A high proportion of survivors have permanent brain damage. … Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis is a late complication of measles. It occurs, on average, 7 years after infection .
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: COMPLICATIONS ARE MORE COMMON AND SEVERE in the CHRONICALLY ILL, CHILDREN UNDER 5, AND ADULTS. ⚠️ MEASLES IN PREGNANCY CAN CAUSE MISCARRIAGE AND PREMATURE DELIVERY, but is NOT ASSOCIATED WITH CONGENITAL MALFORMATION
claims.source_text: people who are chronically ill children <5 years of age adults Measles infection during pregnancy can result in miscarriage and premature delivery. It is not associated with congenital malformation.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ PUBLIC HEALTH: MEASLES IS NOTIFIABLE IN ALL STATES AND TERRITORIES AND IS AN URGENT PUBLIC HEALTH PRIORITY. ⚠️ THERE IS NO SPECIFIC THERAPY FOR ACUTE MEASLES INFECTION
claims.source_text: notifiable disease in all states and territories in Australia, and is an urgent public health priority. … There is no specific therapy for an acute measles infection .
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Measles', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/measles, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ NORMAL HUMAN IMMUNOGLOBULIN DOSING for post-exposure prophylaxis in people who cannot have MMR — infants, pregnant women, the immunocompromised — is in the Handbook's post-exposure table and the CDNA measles guidelines. NEITHER THE TABLE'S DOSES NOR THE CDNA GUIDELINES WERE EXTRACTED.
⚠️ VITAMIN A for measles is not addressed by the retrieved chapter; its absence is not evidence either way.
